learning_outcomes.text: Explain what a communication network is and differentiate between a circuit-switched and a packet-switched network.
List and explain the function of the layers that constitute the OSI and TCP/IP protocol architectures.
Identify the different transmission media and describe their operating characteristics.
Cite encoding schemes for physical level transmission and exemplify their operation.
Specify the functions of the link layer in the TCP/IP architecture related to error, flow, and medium access control.
Identify, explain, and exemplify the protocols used in the link layer of the TCP/IP architecture.
Cite the main communication interfaces, describe their specifications, and exemplify their operation.
Classify network architectures based on their purpose or mobility.

syllabus_topics: Introduction and historical evolution of networks
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 is required on the theoretical exam, and a minimum of 4.5 out of 10 on Practical Exam (P2). If these minimums are met, the final grade is calculated as (0.7 x Theoretical Exam) + (0.3 x (0.35 x P1) + (0.65 x P2)). Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. For the extraordinary call, a minimum of 5 out of 10 in the theoretical part and 4.5 out of 10 in the practical part is required, with the final grade calculated as (0.7 x Theory) + (0.3 x Practical). Otherwise, the final grade will be the minimum of the calculated score and 4.0. The differentiated evaluation follows the same rules as the extraordinary call.
